summary.text: Sydney Kamlager-Dove is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for California's 37th District, first elected in 2022. Born in Chicago and a University of Southern California graduate, she worked in nonprofit arts and community organizations and as a staffer to a state senator before winning local office on the Los Angeles Community College Board in 2015, then the California Assembly (2018) and State Senate (2021). Her House website says she prioritizes land, economic justice, art, and democracy, and she serves on the Foreign Affairs and Judiciary committees.

paragraphs.text: Born in Chicago, Illinois, in 1972; earned a bachelor's degree in political science from the University of Southern California in 1994 and a master's degree in arts management and public policy from Carnegie Mellon University in 1996.

After graduating from USC, worked for Rebuild LA and the Los Angeles Festival, two Los Angeles nonprofits, on job creation and public arts programs, according to her official House biography. Her career also included working as district director for then-State Senator Holly J. Mitchell and in the nonprofit, entertainment, education, and government fields.

Was appointed to the Los Angeles County Commission on Children and Families in 2013 and elected to the Los Angeles Community College Board in 2015, and later served as president of the Los Angeles Community College District Board of Trustees.
Won the April 3, 2018 special election for California State Assembly District 54 outright and served in the Assembly from 2018 to 2021.
Served in the California State Senate (District 30) from 2021 to 2022.
Was elected to the U.S. House in 2022 and took office in January 2023, succeeding Karen Bass in the 37th District.

According to her House website, she is a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, where she is Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on South and Central Asia, and of the House Committee on the Judiciary; she is Whip of the Congressional Black Caucus, Co-Chair of the Congressional Brazil Caucus, and Policy Co-Chair of the Democratic Women's Caucus.

Her House website says that through her Foreign Affairs work she helped secure the release of constituent Eyvin Hernandez, a Los Angeles County public defender detained in Venezuela for nearly two years, and that she passed the GRATEFUL Act on immigration of locally employed U.S. embassy staff.
According to her official biography, she lives in the district with her husband, stepchildren, and a rescue cat.
